1) the lymphatic drainage of the rectum is not uniform, and 2) the drainage of the upper rectum is mainly to the lateral pelvic nodes, while that of the middle and lower rectum is mainly into the retroperitoneal and inferior mesenteric nodes, respectively.
lymph node staging in rectal cancer patients can be improved by the addition of a retroperitoneal and pelvic lymphadenectomy.

the development and application of a new approach to the problem of the optimal design of a system.
the development of a novel, efficient and cost-effective method for the detection and characterization of the lymph nodes in patients with rectal cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the lymphoscintigraphy in the staging of rectal cancer is a very promising tool, but it still requires a more detailed and extensive evaluation.
there is no evidence to support the routine use of lymphadenectomy in the treatment of patients with early stage rectal cancer.

there are many factors to consider before a decision is made on whether a patient should be treated with chemotherapy for advanced colorectal cancer, and the decision should be made by an experienced multidisciplinary team in a specialist colorectal centre.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the lymphatic drainage of rectal adenocancer is more lateral than previously thought, and that the lateral pelvic lymph nodes are not only located at the lateral side of the internal iliac artery, but also in the lateral part of the external iliac artery.
we have shown that a combination of lymphoscintigraphy and SPECT/CT can be used to map lymph nodes and guide the extent of lymphadenectomy for rectal cancer staging.
lymphadenectomy is a critical step in the treatment of rectal cancer, and the lymph nodes should be dissected as extensively as possible.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lymph nodes are not the only source of tumor metastasis in rectal cancer patients.
the use of the lymphoscintigraphic technique in the preoperative staging of rectal cancer is a safe and effective method.
lymphoscintigraphy can be used as a tool to map the extent of the lymphadenectomy and to identify patients who may be candidates for less extensive dissections.
